messages.author: 7dd668eb41c5bfd9
messages.subject: Pystan: Thinning Causes Segmentation Fault
parts: I used to be able to thin my model fits in Pystan and it worked like expected. However, I recently upgraded to Xcode 6 on OS X Mavericks. When I did so, it broke my install of Pystan. I deleted Pystan, reinstalled the new command line tools for Xcode 6, and reinstalled Pystan (2.4.0.3). Now, Pystan/STAN runs like expected unless I try to thin. When I try to thin the posterior samples, the model compiles and runs fine. However, when I try to work with the fit, such as trace plots or extracting coefficients, I get a Segmentation Fault 11 error that crashes Python, which I believe is a memory issue. This happens whether I thin by 5 or 20 and whether I have 1,000 or 100,000 iterations. Why does thinning now cause a memory issue that crashed Python? Did the upgrade to Xcode 6 change something?

messages.author: 17d9c7a6e1a581b8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan: Thinning Causes Segmentation Fault
parts:
Hi Nathan,

I've noticed that XCode 6 seems to break PyStan. As you can tell, code that
works under XCode 5 fails under XCode 6 (gcc and clang). I wonder if the problem
also affects RStan?

I have to imagine this is something with XCode 6 that other people are
encountering for other software as well. From a bit of searching, I see a number
of bugs on Homebrew's list. If you run across a solution or anything pointing in
the direction of a solution, please let me know.

Best wishes,

Allen

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan: Thinning Causes Segmentation Fault
parts:
Hi Nathan,

I missed the bit about thinning and was preoccupied with Xcode 6 problems (of
which there are some real ones).

There was a bug in the extract function that affected thinning. It was fixed in
the development branch. https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/issues/102

Hopefully we'll have a new release shortly
